summary: Describes the Network Time Protocol, which distributes time information across a large internet. It uses a hierarchy of time servers that synchronize each other. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1129 is titled Internet Time Synchronization: The Network Time Protocol. Its listed text file says the RFC is available as PostScript and PDF, but not in ASCII.

subtitle: An RFC titled Internet Time Synchronization: The Network Time Protocol.

tldr.problem: RFC 1129 is titled Internet Time Synchronization: The Network Time Protocol, but the listed text file does not include its technical contents.
tldr.mechanism: The available text states that an ASCII version is unavailable and identifies PostScript and PDF files as the formats in which the RFC is available.
tldr.outcome: The text file supports only the title and archive-format information; it does not provide details of NTP operation.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 1129 as Informational. The available text file says the RFC can be read in PostScript or PDF format.

sections.title: The RFC's Stated Subject
sections.content:
The unit entry gives RFC 1129's title as Internet Time Synchronization: The Network Time Protocol. The listed text file contains no abstract or technical description beyond that title and an archive notice.

Because the supplied text does not include the RFC body, it does not support a description of NTP's design or behavior.
sections.plainLanguage: The title identifies the topic as Internet time synchronization and the Network Time Protocol. The available text does not explain how the protocol works.

sections.title: Available Text Formats
sections.content:
The listed text file states that RFC 1129 is not available in ASCII format. It says the document is available in PostScript and PDF files named rfc1129.ps and rfc1129.pdf.

This is an archive-availability notice rather than the content of the technical memo.
sections.plainLanguage: The archive notice says to use the PostScript or PDF version to read the RFC. The plain-text file contains only that notice.

sections.title: Limits of This Text Copy
sections.content:
The supplied text copy does not include the sections, definitions, or procedures of RFC 1129. No protocol details can be described from this file.

The unit metadata identifies the RFC as Informational, but the technical explanation is not present in the listed source text.
sections.plainLanguage: This text copy does not contain enough information to explain NTP. It only records the title and the available document formats.
